Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:63736
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 1732 of 2024

Appellant :- Vishwajeet Singh
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

And Another
Counsel for Appellant :- Dhirendra Kumar Mishra,Arun Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Sandip Kumar Yadav,Uday Pratap Singh
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.

No one is present on behalf of the opposite party no.2 while the name of Shri Sandip Kumar Yadav
and Shri Uday Pratap Singh is printed in the cause list as counsel for opposite party no.2.

No request
for adjournment has either been moved on behalf of the opposite party no.2.

2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The instant criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the S.C./S.T. Act has been filed by the appellant/Vishwajeet Singh for grant of bail and to set-aside/quash the impugned order dated 15.05.2024 passed by the Special Judge, S.C./S.T. Act, Faizabad/Ayodhya, in Bail Application No.
46 of 2024 (Vishwajeet Singh vs. State of U.P.), arising out of Case Crime No. 420 of 2023, under Sections 308, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. & Section 3(2)Va of the S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Ayodhya/Faizabad, during trial.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant while drawing the attention of this Court towards the first information report as well as the statement of the prosecution witnesses and the medical reports of the three injured persons, vehemently submitted that except one injury, which has been sustained by injured Santosh, all other injuries to the injured Santosh and other injured persons have been found simple and as general role of assault has been assigned to all the accused persons named/charge sheeted at this stage it could not be ascertained as to who from amongst the accused persons was the author of the fatal injury, which has been sustained by the injured on his head.
5. It is further submitted that the charge sheet in this case has been submitted and the offences wherein the charge sheet has been filed, are punishable with up to seven years' of imprisonment.

Appellant is in jail in this case since 15.05.2024 and he is not having any criminal antecedents and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
6.
Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the appellant on the ground that the appellant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

7. Considering the fact that the charged offences wherein the charge sheet has been submitted, are punishable with up to seven years' of imprisonment, only one fatal injury has been shown on the head of injured Santosh and other injured persons have sustained simple injuries and it is argued with considerable force that as general role of assault has been assigned to all the accused persons,
at this stage it could not be ascertained as to who from amongst the accused persons was the author of the fatal injury.
No recovery, etc. has been made on the pointing of the appellant.
Appellant is in jail in this case since 15.05.2024 without any criminal antecedents, a case of bail is emerging in favour of the appellant.
The presence of the appellant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.
8. Thus, for the reasons mentioned above, the impugned order passed by the special court/trial court is set-aside/quashed and the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed.

9. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, let the appellant- Vishwajeet Singh involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The appellant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The appellant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.

11. Identity, status and residence proof of the appellant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
12. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
